name: Open-Elevation API
summary: Elevation in metres for latitude/longitude points worldwide, with a free keyless tier at low volume.
description: Look up ground elevation for one or many coordinates with a GET or POST call. The service is open source and can be self-hosted; the public instance also accepts a dataset selector (for example srtm-250m) and an optional free key for higher monthly limits.

auth.notes: Keyless use is allowed at low volume. A free key (X-API-Key header, or api_key query parameter on GET) raises the monthly quota; the signup form is on the homepage.

rate_limit.summary: Homepage states up to 500 coordinates per month per IP without a key and 1,000 coordinates per month on the free key tier (paid tiers above that). Not enforced in headers I saw.

endpoints.summary: Elevation for pipe-separated lat,lon pairs (request line limited to 1024 bytes)
Elevation for a JSON array of {latitude, longitude} objects (batch)

license.name: Not stated for the dataset; the project code is open source

agent_notes: Locations are latitude,longitude in decimal degrees, results come back in input order with elevation in metres. Use POST for batches. Cache results, the quota is small.
caveats: Free quota is small (500 coordinates per month per IP keyless, as stated on the homepage); a bulk job should self-host or use Open Topo Data.
The homepage mentions paid tiers and a dataset selector; I only ran keyless default-dataset lookups.
The dataset licence is not stated on the homepage.

verification.notes: Keyless GET and a two-point GET and POST lookup answered 200.
